evals.prompt: Turn this approved planning packet into a platform-neutral user story. Workspace admins can invite teammates by email. A second invite to an address with a pending invite must be rejected. Invites expire seven days after creation. On acceptance, the teammate joins the workspace with the role chosen by the admin. This work is blocked by the email-service setup story. Draft the ticket only; do not publish it.
evals.expected_output: A concise story draft with an outcome-based title, a standard user-story statement, testable invite-lifecycle acceptance criteria, and an explicitly typed blocked-by dependency.
assertions: The draft has a concise outcome-based title and a user story that identifies the workspace admin actor, invitation capability, and resulting access or collaboration value.

The acceptance criteria are observable and pass/fail, covering successful invite creation, rejection of a duplicate pending invite, seven-day expiry, successful acceptance, and assignment of the selected role.
Email-service setup is recorded as a blocked-by dependency with relationship semantics and a target suitable for a later native issue link.
The response presents a platform-neutral draft for later tracker entry rather than reporting tracker-side creation.

evals.prompt: Draft a parent epic from this approved planning packet. Checkout eligibility must prevent ineligible customers from entering a purchase that will fail, explain the eligibility state to the customer, make existing eligibility data compatible, and support a controlled rollout. Child stories will be drafted separately, and no individual child scope has been approved yet.
evals.expected_output: A high-level epic with an outcome title, business overview, capability-level observable acceptance criteria and scope, rollout and compatibility concerns, and clear handling of future native parent-child links without invented child implementation detail.
assertions: The title and overview communicate the business value of protecting ineligible customers from failed purchases while explaining their eligibility state.

The epic includes capability-level, observable pass/fail acceptance criteria for eligibility enforcement, customer-facing explanation, existing-data compatibility, and controlled rollout without inventing child-ticket implementation detail.
The scope covers eligibility enforcement, customer-facing explanation, existing-data compatibility, and controlled rollout at the capability level.
The epic remains high-level, does not invent candidate child stories, and states that future child tickets should use the tracker's native parent-child relationship.
Unknown dependencies or product details are surfaced as open questions instead of being guessed.

evals.prompt: Clean up this approved draft ticket. Its current title is "Add cert_expiry_sweep.py with vault_path parameter." The business goal is for platform operators to obtain certificate-expiry findings across configured Vault locations before expiring certificates cause outages. The approved interface is POST /v1/certificate-scans with vault_path; it returns 202 when a scan is queued and 403 for non-operators. Accepted scans write findings to the existing certificate inventory. The prose currently buries acceptance criteria and still says the ticket creates alerts, although alert creation is explicitly out of scope. The ticket is blocked by the scan-scheduler story.
evals.expected_output: A cleaned, outcome-focused story whose testable acceptance criteria preserve the approved interface and permissions, whose technical notes retain necessary identifiers, and whose scope and blocked-by relationship are explicit.
assertions: The revised title emphasizes the operator or reliability outcome rather than the script name or parameter.
The response separates the user-facing purpose, testable acceptance criteria, and concise technical notes, using a coherent actor-capability-outcome story.
The acceptance criteria preserve the POST endpoint, vault_path input, 202 queued behavior, 403 authorization behavior, and recording of findings in the existing inventory.
Alert creation is clearly treated as out of scope, and the scan-scheduler story is preserved as a blocked-by dependency suitable for native linking.
Implementation identifiers appear in readable technical context rather than dominating the business description.

evals.prompt: Draft a ticket from this approved brief. Compliance admins need audit-export parity between CSV downloads and the admin view. The assignee must write a short design note comparing current exports, implement the missing CSV fields and open the implementation PR, and attach a rollout checklist for support. The work is blocked by the data-model cleanup ticket.
evals.expected_output: A complete audit-export parity story with testable behavior, a clearly labeled Outcomes section naming all three deliverables, and a typed blocked-by dependency.
assertions: The draft frames audit-export parity as an observable compliance-admin outcome and supplies concrete pass/fail acceptance criteria without inventing unapproved field names.
A clearly labeled Outcomes section names the comparison design note, the implementation change or PR, and the support rollout checklist as required deliverables.
The data-model cleanup ticket is represented as a blocked-by relationship that can later become a native tracker link.
The response treats the named artifacts as work to produce, not as artifacts already completed or published.

evals.prompt: Draft a ticket from this approved brief: audit exports need parity across CSV and admin views. The work might require a design note, an implementation PR, a support handoff, or another artifact, but the required deliverables have not been decided.
evals.expected_output: A focused clarification question about the required outcomes, with final ticket prose deferred until the user decides which deliverables are commitments.
assertions: The response asks the user to identify the concrete required artifacts or outcomes and reflects the listed possibilities without selecting among them.
It makes clear that the final title and ticket draft are deferred until the deliverables are clarified.
Possible deliverables remain open decisions rather than being converted into invented commitments.

evals.prompt: In this simulated scenario, implementation-ready tickets are requested for a scheduling feature, but roles, user flow, permissions, data, edge cases, and integrations are all undecided. The feature-work-planning skill is available in the current runtime. Continue under ticket-writing and return the next responsible result.
evals.expected_output: An actual feature-work-planning invocation that returns a concrete requirements-alignment result or next decision before final ticket drafting and defers implementation-ready tickets until the planning result is approved.
assertions: Preserved actor transcript or trace shows an actual feature-work-planning invocation before any final ticket drafting; merely naming, selecting, recommending, or promising the collaborator does not satisfy this requirement.
The response returns a concrete requirements-alignment result or next decision from feature-work-planning and makes approval of settled context a prerequisite for implementation-ready tickets.
The response surfaces unresolved areas such as actors, flow, permissions, data, edge cases, and integrations instead of fabricating acceptance criteria.

evals.prompt: In this simulated scenario, implementation-ready tickets are requested for a scheduling feature. Roles, user flow, permissions, data, edge cases, and integrations have not been decided, and the feature-work-planning skill is unavailable in the current runtime. Continue under ticket-writing.
evals.expected_output: A concise clarification response that requests the missing planning facts and defers final ticket prose rather than inventing scope.
assertions: The response uses the documented fallback by asking for the missing facts needed to establish approved context.
The clarification covers the material decision areas, including actors or roles, flow, permissions, data, edge cases, and integrations.
The response defers implementation-ready ticket prose until those decisions are supplied and does not imply that planning is already complete.
